ValveTermsPage.p388: Defined as a relative level of **risk-reduction** provided by a safety function. **Four levels** (SIL1 to SIL4, with 4 being the most dependable) are defined based on probabilistic analysis (FMEA). **IEC 61508 and IEC 61511** standards define functional safety requirements.
ValveTermsPage.p389: Silicon-oxygen backbone elastomer with excellent **high temperature and low temperature properties**.
ValveTermsPage.p390: A valve gate having flat finely finished **parallel faces**, as opposed to a wedge gate. Such a closure element slides across the seats and **does not depend on stem force** (mechanical seal) to achieve tight shut-off.
ValveTermsPage.p391: A device designed to **prevent the clapper of a check valve from slamming** as it closes upon flow reversal. Hydraulic damping cylinders, rotary vanes and torsion springs are all used for this purpose.
ValveTermsPage.p392: An application involving a slurry fluid. **Coal slurry** consisting of about equal parts of coal and water is transported by pipeline from coal mines to power plants.
ValveTermsPage.p393: A **manual arc welding process** that uses a **consumable electrode coated in flux** to lay the weld. The flux coating disintegrates giving off vapors that serve as a **shielding gas** and providing a layer of **slag**.
ValveTermsPage.p394: A substitute natural gas made from the by-products of chemical plants and refineries.
ValveTermsPage.p395: An end connection in which a pipe or tube is inserted into a **counterbored hole** and then brazed or **fillet-welded**.
ValveTermsPage.p396: This term has been cited in this valve handbook under 'SEAT'. A picture of a soft seat arrangement has also been included.
ValveTermsPage.p397: Staggered small cracks formed approximately **perpendicular to the principal stress** (residual and/or applied) resulting in a **'ladder-like' crack array** linking pre-existing **HIC cracks**.
ValveTermsPage.p398: Natural gas containing significant amounts of **hydrogen sulfide ($H_2S$)**. **NACE MR0175 / ISO 15156** presents requirements for material qualification in $H_2S$-containing environments.
ValveTermsPage.p399: Exposure to oilfield environments that contain **$H_2S$** and can cause cracking of materials by the mechanism specifically addressed by **NACE MR0175 / ISO 15156**.
ValveTermsPage.p400: The separation of macroscopic particles from a surface in the form of **flakes or chips**, but also resulting from impacts events.
ValveTermsPage.p401: The ratio of the weight of a given volume of fluid to the weight of an equal volume of water (liquid) or to the weight of an equal volume of air (gas).
ValveTermsPage.p402: It is the ratio between gas specific heat in **constant pressure process ($C_p$)** and specific heat in **constant volume process ($C_v$)**, i.e. $amma = C_p / C_v$.
ValveTermsPage.p403: A flat gasket used between two **RF flanges** (without ring grooves). SPWD gaskets contain a **spiral wound metallic filler** for reinforcement.
ValveTermsPage.p405: The simplest type of gear. In a gear set, the input spur gear and output spur gear are aligned on **parallel shafts**.
ValveTermsPage.p406: Compression of an **O-ring's cross-section** between mating surfaces, noted as both a decimal measurement and as a percentage of the original cross-section. **Radial** compression occurs on the OD and ID. **Axial** compression occurs on the top and bottom surfaces.
ValveTermsPage.p407: A form of **hydrogen induced cracking (HIC)** involving **embrittlement of the metal by atomic hydrogen** that is produced by acid corrosion when exposed to water and **hydrogen sulfide**. **NACE MR0103** defines material requirements for resistance to SSC in sour refinery process environments.
ValveTermsPage.p408: A valve used **underwater** generally in a manifold that will **close and isolate a pipeline or process in an emergency**.
ValveTermsPage.p409: Automatic **wellhead valve assembly** which **closes upon loss of power supply**.
ValveTermsPage.p410: A rod or shaft used to **transmit motion from an operator to the closure element** of a valve.
ValveTermsPage.p411: Assembly consisting of the stem extension and the stem extension housing.
ValveTermsPage.p412: A position indicating rod supplied with gate valves. It extends from the top of the valve stem and serves to indicate the relative position of the gate. Also termed **VPI (Valve Position Indicator)**.
ValveTermsPage.p413: A one or two-piece nut which engages the stem threads of a valve and **transmits torque from an operator to the valve stem**.
ValveTermsPage.p414: The collar on a ball valve which **restricts the ball to quarter rotation** from the fully open to the fully closed position. See Key Stop.
ValveTermsPage.p415: A procedure used to **isolate a section of line in the absence of a shut-off valve**. After welding a flanged saddle, the line is **'hot tapped'** and an expanding resilient plug is inserted into the pipe bore.
ValveTermsPage.p416: A device used to measure **deformation (strain)** of an object. The most common type consists of a metallic foil pattern whose **electrical resistance changes** as the object is deformed.
ValveTermsPage.p417: Defined as **force per unit area ($F/A$)**, stress is a measure of the intensity of internal forces acting within a body.
ValveTermsPage.p418: Measured as a **percentage increase in the inside diameter (ID) of an O-ring**. Stretch results in a reduction and flattening of the seal's cross-section. There are two types: **installation stretch** and **assembly stretch**.
ValveTermsPage.p419: A bolt **threaded on both ends** used in bolting together two members.
ValveTermsPage.p420: Flanged end or outlet connection in which **thread-anchored studs screwed into tapped holes replace the holes for bolt studs**.
ValveTermsPage.p421: The **annular chamber** provided around a valve stem in a sealing system into which **deformable packing** is introduced.
ValveTermsPage.p422: Metal structure which provides a stable footing when the valve is set on a fixed base.
ValveTermsPage.p423: Average value of exterior roughness often expressed in microinches i.e **RMS (Root Mean Square)** or **Ra (Roughness Arithmetic Average)**.
ValveTermsPage.p424: A transient sudden **rise of pressure in a pipeline**. Caused most frequently by the **sudden closure of a block valve** or **emergency shutdown of a pump**.
ValveTermsPage.p425: A valve designed to **relieve pressure surges in liquid pipelines** thus preventing line rupture due to transient pressures exceeding design limits.
ValveTermsPage.p426: A media temperature that the valve is only required to **survive in typically for a duration of time**. The valve is **not meant to be operated** at this temperature.
ValveTermsPage.p427: A tool for bending or forming cold metal to a required shape.
ValveTermsPage.p428: Cracking that **connects hydrogen-induced cracks (HIC)** on adjacent planes in a steel.
ValveTermsPage.p429: Natural gas that **does not contain hydrogen sulfide ($H_2S$)** or significant quantities of carbon dioxide ($CO_2$).
ValveTermsPage.p430: **Volumetric increase** of an elastomeric material when in contact with a fluid.
ValveTermsPage.p431: A check valve in which the closure element is a **hinged clapper** which swings or rotates about a supporting shaft. See Check Valve.
ValveTermsPage.p432: Form of **SSC** that may occur when a steel contains a local **'soft zone'** of low yield strength material.
ValveTermsPage.p433: A pipe or tubing fitting with a side outlet at **right angles**. Resembles a 'T'.
ValveTermsPage.p434: The **maximum amount of tensile stress** (ultimate strength) that a material can withstand before failure or rupture occurs.
ValveTermsPage.p435: A test performed on a specially machined specimen to determine physical properties e.g. **yield strength, ultimate strength and percent elongation**.
ValveTermsPage.p437: Documents provided by a manufacturer certifying that required tests were performed.
ValveTermsPage.p438: For **relieving pressure in vessels/tubing due to temperature changes**.
ValveTermsPage.p439: The **intentional restriction of flow** by partially closing or opening a valve. A wide range of throttling is accomplished automatically in regulators and control valves.
ValveTermsPage.p440: Characterizes valves in the open position where the bore presents a **smooth uninterrupted interior surface** across seat rings, affording **minimum pressure drop**. There are no cavities that can accumulate debris or impede pipeline cleaning equipment ('pigging').
ValveTermsPage.p441: A valve designed and constructed to allow for **installation/removal of the internal parts (trim) while the valve remains installed in a pipeline**. It is specifically designed for **in-line maintenance**.
ValveTermsPage.p442: The turning effort required to operate a valve. Usually expressed in **pound-feet or N-m** and referred to the stem nut handwheel or operator pinion shaft.
ValveTermsPage.p443: An electrical device on a motor operator which **cuts off power to the operator when allowable torque is exceeded**, thus preventing damage to the valve and/or the operator.
ValveTermsPage.p444: A coiled spring which exerts a force by **twisting about its axis** rather than by compression or elongation.
ValveTermsPage.p445: A length of pipe that is welded to a valve hub or closure. It serves as a transition from the customer's piping to the valve to **compensate for differences in material or size**. (Also known as **Pups**).
ValveTermsPage.p446: A main pipeline transporting oil or gas from wells or storage fields to refineries, loading docks or distribution companies.
ValveTermsPage.p447: The displacement of the closure member from the closed position. For a rotary control valve is the **angle between the closed and the actual position**. The fully open position is identified as **rated travel**.
ValveTermsPage.p448: Those parts (and their materials) of a valve assembly **excluding the valve body, bonnet assembly**, which are **exposed and in contact with the line medium**. Usually consisting of the seat rings, valve ball/obturator and stem.
ValveTermsPage.p449: A particular design of a butterfly valve (triple offset) where the stem is located behind the disc below the centerline of the disc and its cone axis is **offset from the centerline of the disc**. This design is capable of a **very tight shut-off** at temperatures well above 1000F 530C).
ValveTermsPage.p450: That part of a ball valve which **holds the ball on a fixed vertical axis** and about which the ball turns. The torque requirement of a trunnion-mounted ball valve is **significantly less** than that for a floating ball design.
ValveTermsPage.p451: The random flow of a fluid in which the **velocity at a certain point in the fluid varies irregularly**.
ValveTermsPage.p452: A term used to describe the **ratio between the minimum and maximum flow conditions** seen in a particular system. This term is sometimes incorrectly applied to valves. See **Rangeability**.
ValveTermsPage.p453: The **number of complete revolutions** of a handwheel or the pinion shaft of a gear operator required to stroke a valve from fully open to fully closed or vice versa.
ValveTermsPage.p454: A **non-destructive inspection procedure (NDE)** using **high frequency sound waves** to detect **voids and imperfections** throughout the thickness of metal parts. Techniques and procedures are covered in **ASME V, Art. 4, Art. 5, and ASTM A388, A435 and A577**.
ValveTermsPage.p455: Valve designed for **blocking the flow in one direction only**.
ValveTermsPage.p456: A small **3-piece fitting** used to join two lengths of pipe. The connection is **mechanically sealed by an external nut**.
ValveTermsPage.p457: A device which **controls or isolates the flow** of a liquid or gas in a conduit or pipeline.
ValveTermsPage.p458: Size determination for a control valve for given process conditions shall be carried out in accordance with **IEC standards**, which specify the prediction method of the achievable **capacity** for any size and style of control valve.
ValveTermsPage.p459: The pressure of a vapor in natural **thermodynamic equilibrium with its condensed phase** in a closed system. Vapor pressure **varies with temperature**.
ValveTermsPage.p460: A small variable profile valve put in a flow line and used with a **pilot** to restrict the flow into the pilot and make the pilot **more or less sensitive to changing conditions**.
ValveTermsPage.p461: A data sheet defining the minimum level of a valve design requirements including the **materials, testing, inspection and certification**.
ValveTermsPage.p463: The portion of a flow stream where **fluid velocity is at its maximum** and **fluid static pressure and the cross-sectional area are at their minimum**. In a control valve, the vena contracta normally occurs just **downstream of the actual physical restriction**.
ValveTermsPage.p464: A special pipe plug having a small allen-wrench operated vent valve. Located at the bottom of most ball valves. Used to **vent the body cavity pressure** (when the line valve is closed) to check seat seal tightness or perform minor repairs. Can be removed to blow out debris. See **Block and Bleed** and **Drain Plug**.
ValveTermsPage.p465: A **reduced bore valve** having a bore smaller in diameter than the inlet or outlet. The flow through a venturi valve will be reduced because of the smaller port.
ValveTermsPage.p466: A standard method for measuring the **hardness of metals** (particularly those with extremely hard surfaces). The surface is subjected to pressure by a **pyramid-shaped diamond**. Hardness is determined from the **diagonal of the resulting indention**.
ValveTermsPage.p467: A measure of the **internal friction of a fluid** or the **resistance of a fluid to flow**. Two fluids of identical specific gravity may have quite different viscosities.
ValveTermsPage.p468: Examination of parts and equipment for **visible defects** in material and workmanship.
ValveTermsPage.p470: Examination for **internal material defects** by methods such as **radiographic and/or ultrasonic testing**.
ValveTermsPage.p472: The thickness of the wall of a **pressure vessel or of a pipe**.
ValveTermsPage.p473: The physical effect often accompanied by loud banging produced by **pressure waves** generated within the piping by **rapid change of velocity** in a liquid system.
ValveTermsPage.p474: The end connection of a valve which is to be installed by **welding into the line**. To prepare the end bevel, it is necessary to know the wall thickness and specified minimum yield strength of the connecting pipe. See **End Bevel**.
ValveTermsPage.p475: Damage to a solid surface generally involving **progressive loss of material** due to **relative motion** between that surface and a contacting substance or substances.
ValveTermsPage.p476: Verification of a component's **resistance under specific wear conditions**.
ValveTermsPage.p477: Of a device that is **protected against intrusion of water, sand, dust or other atmospheric contamination**.
ValveTermsPage.p478: A gate whose seating surfaces are **inclined to the direction of closing thrust** so that mechanical force on the stem produces tight contact with the inclined seat rings. Manufactured to **API 600**.
ValveTermsPage.p480: A flanged piping element with a weld-neck used to provide a **companion flange for installation of flanged valves**. Also used to convert weld end valves to flanged valves or vice versa.
ValveTermsPage.p481: A reducing fitting used on weld end piping components to **adapt from a large sized pipe to a smaller diameter pipe or vice versa**.
ValveTermsPage.p482: The operation of a valve by means of a **handle or lever**. Used on **smaller size and lower pressure class valves**.
ValveTermsPage.p483: Used in connection with a pressure rating. **100 WOG** indicates that the rated pressure is **100 psi** in water, oil or gas service at normal ambient temperatures.
ValveTermsPage.p484: Gears used to transmit motion or power between **right angle shafts** when a **high-ratio reduction is necessary**. The worm is the small gear which drives the larger ring gear. See **BGO (Bevel Gear Operated)**.
ValveTermsPage.p485: The pressure at which a valve is **designed to operate**. Same as operating pressure rating.
ValveTermsPage.p486: Products shaped by means of **forging** or **hot isostatic pressing**.
ValveTermsPage.p488: The **limiting stress** beyond which a material will sustain **permanent deformation**. Up to the yield strength, the material will spring back to its original dimension when the applied stress is removed.
ValveTermsPage.p489: That part of a gate valve which serves as a **spacer** between the **bonnet** and the **operator or actuator**.
ValveTermsPage.p490: A measure of **stiffness** (modulus of elasticity, elastic modulus, or tensile modulus). Defined as the ratio, for small strains, of the **rate of change of stress with strain** ($ rac{elta igma}{elta arepsilon}$). Determined from the slope of a stress-strain curve during tensile testing.

ControlTermsPage.title: SECTION 2 : Actuator & Control Systems Terms & Definitions
ControlTermsPage.p1: Electricity which periodically reverses direction. Unit of measurement **Hz. (cycles per second)**.
ControlTermsPage.p2: A vessel in which a **gas is enclosed and compressed by the liquid** in a hydraulic system, thus **storing energy** to supply liquid under pressure to the system when needed. Types available are **bladder, piston and diaphragm**.
ControlTermsPage.p3: A device attached to a valve to provide the operation. Motion energy can be **pneumatic, hydraulic, electric or manual or a combination**. Types include: Spring Return, Double Acting, Direct Gas, Gas/Hydraulic, Positioning/Modulating. All the above can be fitted to **quarter turn or linear acting valves**.
ControlTermsPage.p4: A term used to describe the **interface between the valve and the valve actuator** when the actuator device **cannot be directly bolted** to the valve top-work flange. Can be a simple plate or a fabricated pedestal.
ControlTermsPage.p5: A container (vessel) in which **gas is stored under pressure** as a source of pneumatic fluid power.
ControlTermsPage.p6: Representation by means of a **continuously variable physical quantity**. Typical analogue control or measured variable signal is **4...20mA**.
ControlTermsPage.p7: The name given to the framework for controlling **explosive atmospheres** and the standards of equipment and protective systems used in them. It is based on the requirements of **European Directives 99/92/EC and 94/9/EC**.
ControlTermsPage.p8: A separating device to **insulate or isolate electrical circuits**. Also the separating device in gas/hydraulic systems.
ControlTermsPage.p9: A highly visible device to show **open/closed valve status**, usually incorporates **limit switches**.
ControlTermsPage.p10: The dimension of a circle of tapped or through holes on a valve top flange or actuator mounting plate for **securing the two devices**.
ControlTermsPage.p11: A device to **increase air pressure and volume**, usually between a low volume pilot supply and a large actuator cylinder.
ControlTermsPage.p12: Permits **air movement between atmosphere and the component** in which it is fitted.
ControlTermsPage.p13: A chain operated wheel attached to a manual actuator with a closed loop of chain to enable the **operation of an overhead valve**.
ControlTermsPage.p14: Insulated wire is wound onto a spool through which **electric current is passed to create a magnetic field**. See **Solenoid**.
ControlTermsPage.p15: A device which converts **mechanical power or force to pneumatic fluid power**.
ControlTermsPage.p16: The time to actuate a valve from **open to close**. Time normally specified by the required process conditions and can be adjustable.
ControlTermsPage.p17: The motive force for a pneumatic or hydraulic actuator is generated by a **plunger or piston being pressurized** inside a cylindrical housing.
ControlTermsPage.p18: A **single-cable link** which provides **communication between control stations** which are physically separated.
ControlTermsPage.p19: The amount of power supply (or signal range) of an actuator can be varied **without initiating valve obturator motion**. The technical term for deadband is **hysteresis**.
ControlTermsPage.p20: A spring-return device which **maintains the position of the spool** of a directional control valve in position.
ControlTermsPage.p21: Data represented by a **series of digits**. Many functions/values can be transmitted over a single pair of cables.
ControlTermsPage.p22: Electricity which **flows in one direction** as produced by a battery.
ControlTermsPage.p23: The amount of fluid transferred during a **single operation of an actuator cylinder**.
ControlTermsPage.p24: Central process control system distributed among **two or more process control units** coupled by a **high speed communications network**. Remote field devices (actuators) are connected to one of the process control units.
ControlTermsPage.p25: An actuator which **requires power in both operating directions** (i.e. no spring).
ControlTermsPage.p26: An electromechanical device that uses an **electric motor to drive through a gearbox** to an output shaft which is connected to a valve stem.
ControlTermsPage.p27: A hydraulic actuator powered from an **integrally mounted hydraulic power unit** requiring only an **electrical supply and control signal**.
ControlTermsPage.p28: The ability of an equipment or system to function satisfactorily in an electromagnetic environment **without introducing intolerable electromagnetic disturbances** (IEC definition).
ControlTermsPage.p29: The actuation of a valve by **electric motor**.
ControlTermsPage.p30: Housings for control equipment to provide **protection appropriate to the environment**. Designed to meet the requirements of **I.E.C. and/or N.E.M.A.**.
ControlTermsPage.p31: Mechanical device to **limit the open and closed position** of the actuator.
ControlTermsPage.p32: Surface treatment of metal to **protect against corrosion**.
ControlTermsPage.p33: A term used to describe the desired **failure position of a control valve**: **fail-closed, fail-open, or fail-in-place**. Fail-in-place usually requires the use of a **lock-up valve** with a spring-return actuator.
ControlTermsPage.p34: The process of **transferring data from the output of a system to the input** typically for **valve position monitoring**.
ControlTermsPage.p35: A **digital, serial, two-way communications system** that interconnects measurement and control devices (sensors, actuators, controllers). Allows for **calibration, diagnostics and decentralised control**.
ControlTermsPage.p36: A device incorporated into a system to **remove contaminants from the fluid**.
ControlTermsPage.p38: A procedure for hydraulic systems of cleaning the fluid to a predetermined standard. **NAS (National Aeronautical Standard) 1638** is typically used, with **NAS 6** being the most common requirement.
ControlTermsPage.p39: The centre enclosure of the actuator housing the **Scotch Yoke Mechanism**.
ControlTermsPage.p40: A liquid filled glass device for **detecting high temperature**. At a predetermined temperature the bulb **fractures** causing the control valve to change state and signal the actuator to close the valve.
ControlTermsPage.p42: For pipelines where **high pressure gas is used to displace hydraulic fluid** into the actuator.
ControlTermsPage.p43: In electric actuators, it is a **lost motion mechanism** to allow a motor to reach full speed before engaging the gear drive. Provides a higher efficiency for overcoming valve **break torque**.
ControlTermsPage.p45: The **manual effort (force)** required on the rim of a handwheel to open or close the valve. Normally expressed in **Newton ($N$)**.
ControlTermsPage.p46: A **bi-directional industrial field communication protocol** used to communicate between intelligent field instruments and host systems.
ControlTermsPage.p47: Locations where hazardous materials will require electrical equipment to have **special protection to prevent causing an explosion**.
ControlTermsPage.p48: The **vertical distance between two levels** in a liquid (related to pressure).
ControlTermsPage.p49: Cylindrical in form with the teeth having a constant section and cut along a **helix** on the pitch diameter.
ControlTermsPage.p50: Constructed such that there is **zero ingress** against entry of air or other gasses, **moisture or dust**.
ControlTermsPage.p51: A device that converts **hydraulic pressure into motion** via a pressurized piston within a cylinder. This linear movement is converted into rotary movement for quarter turn valves by a **scotch yoke mechanism**.
ControlTermsPage.p52: A device by which **rotation of an hydraulically powered motor is converted into mechanical motion**.
ControlTermsPage.p53: A device to **create kinetic energy within a hydraulic system**. Usually comprises a motor, a storage tank, filters, regulators, directional valves, gauges etc. to power one or multiple valve actuators.
ControlTermsPage.p54: A device which converts **low pressure fluid power into a higher pressure**. See **Booster**.
ControlTermsPage.p55: A mechanism which **prevents the operation of a device** until **certain conditions have been satisfied**. Normally electrical or mechanical safety devices.
ControlTermsPage.p56: A circuit in which any thermal effect or spark is **not capable of causing ignition of flammable gas or material**.
ControlTermsPage.p57: A device which converts **DC voltage to AC voltage**.
ControlTermsPage.p58: The **degree of protection an enclosure provides** against the ingress of solids and water.
ControlTermsPage.p59: **Instrument Society of America** (now ISA - International Society of Automation).
ControlTermsPage.p60: A function that provides **momentary operation of an actuator** to achieve a **small movement** of the valve.
ControlTermsPage.p61: An epoxy-based **intumescent coating** to provide **fire protection**. Works by **endothermic reaction** rather than insulation.
ControlTermsPage.p62: Switches which are actuated at preset values by the movement of the valve. Normally **fully open or closed positions**, but can be set at intermediate points. Types include **mechanical, magnetic (reed) and proximity**.
ControlTermsPage.p63: A system incorporating a pressure transmitter to sense the **rate of pressure drop in a pipeline**. When the rate of pressure drop falls outside a preset value, the control system will **close the valve**. Can be electrical or mechanical.
ControlTermsPage.p64: A device that develops **force and motion** (e.g., stem movement), from an available energy source, **in a linear manner**, as opposed to rotationally like an electric motor.
ControlTermsPage.p65: A device that **adds controlled amounts of lubricant** to a fluid power system.
ControlTermsPage.p66: A device used in modulating service to provide **position feedback of the valve position**. Provides an **electrical output proportional to valve position**.
ControlTermsPage.p68: A published torque value of the **maximum torque that may be applied to a valve stem** before **permanent deformation** may occur. The actuator maximum torque must not exceed this figure.
ControlTermsPage.p69: A term for describing the method of **controlling flow through a valve by varying the pressure drop** across it, allowing for intermediate positioning.
ControlTermsPage.p70: A device which converts **electric, pneumatic or fluid power into mechanical force and motion**, normally a rotating shaft output.
ControlTermsPage.p71: An American consensus standard for the **installation of electrical systems (National Electrical Code)**.
ControlTermsPage.p73: **National Pipe Thread Standard** for **tapered threads** - American.
ControlTermsPage.p74: A **manual mechanical or hydraulic device** fitted to an actuator for **operating the valve when the normal motive power is not available**.
ControlTermsPage.p75: An actuator which delivers torque for **rotation of less than one revolution** to the valve. Typically used for **ball, butterfly and plug valves**.
ControlTermsPage.p76: A manual or automatic procedure to **partially close a valve to prove operation integrity** without affecting the process.
ControlTermsPage.p77: The European Directive **97/23/EC** for pressure equipment. All items placed on the market after May 2002 must comply and carry the **CE marking**.
ControlTermsPage.p78: The **alternate on-off periods of operation** of an actuator (electric) as specified in the rating.
ControlTermsPage.p79: The device which prevents operation of an electric actuator motor if the **3 phases are not connected in the correct rotation**.
ControlTermsPage.p80: A device in which **energy from a control system is amplified by energy from another source** to power the actuator.
ControlTermsPage.p81: The device used for **converting fluid power to mechanical energy** within a cylinder.
ControlTermsPage.p82: An electrical term which **determines the direction of current flow** in an electrical circuit.
ControlTermsPage.p83: A device for giving a **continuous electrical output of valve position**. Can be **analogue or digital** format.
ControlTermsPage.p84: Using the actuator to **modulate the valve** (set it to an intermediate position).
ControlTermsPage.p85: A device which receives a pneumatic or electrical **command signal**, **compares it to the actual valve stem position**, and converts the difference into a signal to the actuator to **adjust the valve position**.
ControlTermsPage.p86: Its operation uses a **voltage gradient** across a resistive element which has a variable pick-off point connected to the valve stem. Stem movement changes the voltage to provide an **electrical output of the valve position**.
ControlTermsPage.p87: The device which **provides power** to a control system or component.
ControlTermsPage.p88: A definition of the **rules by which master and slave units communicate** with each other.
ControlTermsPage.p89: A device that **detects the presence of a target** by it disturbing the associated magnetic field. Used as a limit switch and suitable for **intrinsically safe circuits**.
ControlTermsPage.p90: A **one-way valve** connected directly to the actuator cylinder with a **large exhaust port** to allow **fast dumping of air** from the cylinder (to speed up operation).
ControlTermsPage.p91: The **probability that a device will operate correctly** over a specified period or amount of usage.
ControlTermsPage.p92: The **closeness of the band of measurements** of repeated measurements of the same variable under the same operating conditions.
ControlTermsPage.p93: In hydraulic systems, it is the **storage tank for unpressurised fluid** from which the pump draws its supply. It is also the vessel to which the **return lines are connected**.
ControlTermsPage.p94: The time between an **instruction to proceed with an action** to the **completion of the task**.
ControlTermsPage.p95: Is a factor applied to the nominal operating torque or thrust given by the valve manufacturer. Can be **between 1.2 and 2.0** depending on application (provides a power margin).
ControlTermsPage.p96: The mechanism within a quarter turn actuator for **converting linear movement to 90 deg rotary output**. Several yoke configurations (cants) allow selection of the actuator output torque to best suit the valve torque characteristic.
ControlTermsPage.p97: The process of **operating a new spring several times prior to installation** into a spring can. Assures optimum spring performance from first operation of the actuator.
ControlTermsPage.p98: Handwheel operators and electric actuators can be **side mounted on a valve** and driven through a **bevel gearbox** to allow **easier operator access**.
ControlTermsPage.p99: A device to **reduce the gas flow noise** by tuned resonant control of gas expansion.
ControlTermsPage.p100: Passive or defined **low energy devices** generating less than **1.5V, 100mA, 25mW**.
ControlTermsPage.p102: The pressure stated as the fluid pressure available to **size the actuator** to operate the valve.
ControlTermsPage.p103: An actuator or positioner which includes a **microprocessor** for communicating with a central control system and to **make local control decisions**, distributing part of the control function normally performed in the central DCS.
ControlTermsPage.p104: A device that turns an **electrical signal sent to a coil into a mechanical movement** inside the valve, thus allowing it to control the flow of liquid and gases. Often used in the control piping of powered hydraulic or pneumatic cylinder operators.
ControlTermsPage.p105: A 2-port valve (usually a **needle valve**) for **restricting the flow into or out of an actuator** to **adjust the operating time**.
ControlTermsPage.p106: The **welded enclosure** containing the **compressed spring** (in spring-return actuators).
ControlTermsPage.p107: An actuator which **requires power in one direction** with a **spring operating in the other direction** (to fail to a safe position). See **Actuator**.
ControlTermsPage.p108: A combination of **friction and adhesion (sticking)** that must be **overcome to move a device from rest**.
ControlTermsPage.p109: A **force transmitted by an actuator to a valve** through the valve stem expressed in **Newton ($N$)** or **Pounds ($lbs$)**.
ControlTermsPage.p110:
* **STO (Start-To-Open):** Thrust required to **start movement** from closed.
* **ETO (End-To-Open):** Thrust required to **fully open** the valve.
* **STC (Start-To-Close):** Thrust required to **start movement** from open.
* **ETC (End-To-Close):** Thrust required to **fully close** the valve.

**Note:** Always check whether the valve is standard acting or reverse acting.
ControlTermsPage.p111:
* **BTO (Break-To-Open):** Torque required to **start movement** from closed.
* **RTO (Run-To-Open):** Torque required for **travel** in the opening direction.
* **ETO (End-To-Open):** Torque required to **fully open** the valve.
* **BTC (Break-To-Close):** Torque required to **start movement** from open.
* **RTC (Run-To-Close):** Torque required for **travel** in the closing direction.
* **ETC (End-To-Close):** Torque required to **fully close** the valve.
ControlTermsPage.p112: The torque output of an actuator normally expressed in **Nm** or **foot/lbs**.
ControlTermsPage.p114: Applied to **high integrity control systems** where a valve closure requires **more than one command signal to operate**. Typically **2 out of 3 (2oo3)** to alleviate a single component failure.

CommercialTermsPage.title: SECTION 3 : Commercial Terms
CommercialTermsPage.p115: Guarantee furnished by a bank that in the event of **nonperformance of an agreement**, it will **reimburse the customer for the amount paid** (the advance payment).
CommercialTermsPage.p116: Documentary credit which is granted to **another beneficiary** on the basis of an existing, **non-transferrable** documentary credit (**prime/master/original letter of credit**). Commonly used by middlemen when the original credit cannot be transferred and/or the terms of the two credits are not the same. Also termed **Counter Credit**.
CommercialTermsPage.p117: **Irrevocable commitment of a bank to make payment** if the seller **fails to supply specific goods or services**. Main types include: **Bid Bond, Performance Bond, Advance Payment Bond, Payment Guarantee, and Credit Guarantee**.
CommercialTermsPage.p118: A **surety bond** filed by contractors, guaranteeing that in the event a bid is accepted, the successful contractor will **sign the contract and furnish a Performance Bond**.
CommercialTermsPage.p119: A document **evidencing the receipt of goods for shipment** and issued by a freight carrier. The document evidences **control of goods**, serves as a **receipt** for the merchandise, and as evidence of the carrier's **obligation to transport the goods** to their proper destination.
CommercialTermsPage.p120: (... named port of destination). An **Incoterm** requiring the seller to deliver when the **goods pass the ship's rail in the port of shipment**. The seller pays costs and freight to the named port, but the **risk of loss or damage transfers to the buyer** upon passing the ship's rail. Seller must **clear goods for export**. Used only for **sea or inland waterway transport**.
CommercialTermsPage.p121: (... named port of destination). An **Incoterm**. Similar to CFR, but the **seller must also procure marine insurance** against the buyer's risk of loss or damage during carriage. **Risk transfers to the buyer upon passing the ship's rail**. Seller is responsible for **export clearance**. Used only for **sea and inland waterway transport**.
CommercialTermsPage.p122: (... named place of destination). An **Incoterm**. The seller delivers the goods to the **nominated carrier**, pays the **cost of carriage to the destination**, and **procures insurance** against the buyer's risk. The **buyer bears all risks** after delivery to the carrier. Seller is responsible for **export clearance**. May be used irrespective of the **mode of transport** (multimodal).
CommercialTermsPage.p123: (... named place of destination). An **Incoterm**. The seller delivers the goods to the **nominated carrier** and pays the **cost of carriage to the destination**. The **buyer bears all risks and additional costs** occurring after the goods are delivered to the carrier. Seller is responsible for **export clearance**. May be used irrespective of the **mode of transport** (multimodal).
CommercialTermsPage.p124: A guarantee to secure the **lender's claim on the borrower** in the event of the **loan not being repaid** as stipulated in the Agreement.
CommercialTermsPage.p125: (... named place of destination). An **Incoterm** representing the **maximum obligation for the seller**. The seller delivers the goods to the buyer, **cleared for import** and not unloaded. The seller bears **all costs and risks**, including any **duty for import** in the country of destination.
CommercialTermsPage.p126: (... named place of destination). An **Incoterm**. The seller delivers the goods to the buyer, **not cleared for import** and not unloaded. The seller bears all costs and risks, **other than any duty for import**, which is borne by the buyer.
CommercialTermsPage.p127: **Special packing and crating** that is required for export shipping. Includes **sealing against a salt atmosphere** (sea air).
CommercialTermsPage.p128: (... named place). An **Incoterm** representing the **minimum obligation for the seller**. The seller delivers when the goods are placed at the buyer's disposal at the seller's premises or another named place, **not cleared for export** and not loaded on any collecting vehicle.
CommercialTermsPage.p129: (... named port of shipment). An **Incoterm**. The seller delivers when goods are placed **alongside the vessel** at the named port of shipment. The **buyer bears all costs and risks** of loss or damage to the goods from that moment. Seller must **clear goods for export**.
CommercialTermsPage.p130: (... named place). An **Incoterm**. The seller delivers the goods, **cleared for export**, to the **carrier nominated by the buyer** at the named place. **Risk transfers to the buyer upon delivery to the carrier** or nominated person.
CommercialTermsPage.p131: (... named port of shipment). An **Incoterm**. The seller delivers when the **goods pass the ship's rail at the named port of shipment**. The **buyer bears all costs and risks** of loss or damage from that point. Seller must **clear goods for export**. Used only for **sea or inland waterway transport**.
CommercialTermsPage.p132: **Standard trade definitions** most commonly used in **international sales contracts**. Devised and published by the **International Chamber of Commerce (ICC)**.
CommercialTermsPage.p133: A binding document that a buyer can request from his bank to **guarantee that the payment for goods will be transferred to the seller** upon the seller presenting the **necessary shipping documents** confirming the delivery. Technical term is **Documentary Credit**.
CommercialTermsPage.p134: A guarantee that secures any **claims by the seller on the buyer for payment** of the contract price by the agreed date. Often used instead of a documentary credit where delivery is against **'open account'**.
CommercialTermsPage.p135: A bond, usually issued by a bank, **guaranteeing specific monetary payment to a beneficiary** if the purchaser or maker **fails to perform or acts in violation of a contract**.
